work.text: A trained checkpoint: the saved weights of a coding model, uploaded to a private bucket and signalled on chain. The subnet pays whoever holds or recently held the crown, so the thing produced is a model that beats the reigning king in a duel.
work.quote: King-of-the-hill subnet. Miners upload checkpoints privately to a validator-controlled bucket

scoring.text: One duel, challenger against king, over 1,300 turns of a coding corpus. A frozen teacher model scores each turn as min(R, G): R is how much the miner's written reasoning helps the teacher predict the right action, G is whether that reasoning sits inside the teacher's own band. The challenger crowns only if its mean margin clears max(2 standard errors, 0.002).
scoring.quote: Per turn: turn = min(R, G); paired mean(turn_c - turn_k) > max(k_sigma * SE, min_margin)
scoring.disagrees: llms.txt on 2026-09-20 opens with a newer meter, min(z_R, typ_c, z_A) with a floor of 0.2 teacher sd, while its own fork history and the repository at the pinned commit give min(R, G) with the 0.002 floor and n_turns = 1300 in affine/affine.toml.

split.text: Not proportional. Every crown won in the last 72 hours gets one equal share of the miner emission, whether or not it still holds the throne. A crown older than 72 hours earns nothing. When no crown is inside the window, the share goes to the burn UID. Effective 2026-09-14.
split.quote: a crown is paid for at most 72 hours; every crown inside its window gets one equal share
split.disagrees: The repository at the pinned commit of 2026-09-10 pays equal shares to the current king and prior distinct kings with no time window (affine/affine/chain.py, set_rolling_weights); the 72-hour rule postdates the commit, and the payout module llms.txt cites is published on Hippius, not GitHub.

judges.text: Three validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot, of 64 permitted. Weights are committed then revealed, at most once per 100 blocks. The validator does the work itself: it rents a GPU pod, loads both checkpoints, runs the whole duel, and seeds it from the reveal-block hash so anyone can replay the verdict. Nothing is sampled.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100, max_validators 64; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 3

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The puzzle turns per duel, not per epoch: a challenger is evaluated when it reaches the front of the queue, and a crown stands until a challenger clears the bar. The snapshot on 2026-09-20 showed reign 20. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 5,000 blocks, about 16 hours.

buyer.text: Nobody is named. The front page offers a chat box with the reigning model, and every crowned checkpoint is free to download with a signed manifest. There is no price, no customer and no usage figure on the site, in llms.txt or in the repository. The miner's income is emission.
buyer.quote: Talk directly to the reigning SN120 king

exploits.text: The program records its own hacks. A king was crowned on a constant filler suffix and scored 0 of 50 on the bench, which is why the score became min(R, G). Reign 13, a re-upload of reign 12's weights, won on noise and was uncrowned. Defences: one evaluation slot per hotkey, burned at enqueue; identical weights rejected as copies; a published exploit audit after every crowning that can revert it.
exploits.quote: wvk-9 king crowned on a constant filler suffix and benched 0/50
